There's a trick to getting these pens not to leak globs of paint everywhere when you first get them. You have to hold the pen with the point upwards, towards the ceiling, push the nib in with your finger, you'll hear a small amount of air escape, like a hissing sound. Then turn back over and press repeatedly onto paper to get the paint going. If you don't do this, globs will come out and go everywhere! Happened to me and lots of paint was wasted. But they work great once you get them going correctly.

Posca pens are awesome...plain & simple.  I will re-interate what someone else said about using ANY kind of paint pen because I think this is invaluable information. PAINT PENS LEAK IF NOT STARTED PROPERLY!!!!  Many people complain of paint pens leaking big blobs after the fist couple of uses. It's a real issue! Here's the trick (at least as far as I know)... SHAKE THE PEN LIKE CRAZY. HOLD THE PEN UPRIGHT . PUT IT UP TO YOUR EAR, THEN HOLD DOWN THE NIB WITH YOUR FINGER TIP OR FINGER NAIL. YOU WILL HEAR A LITTLE CLICK & HISS. HOLD IT DOWN FOR 10 SECONDS. (Yes, count to 10 SLOWLY.) THEN FLIP THE PEN AND VERY GRADUALLY WORK THE PAINT INTO THE FRESH NIB BY PRESSING DOWN HALF WAY. BE GENTLE. BE PATIENT. LITTLE PRESSES UNTIL YOU SEE THE PAINT HAS FILLED THE NIB AND PAINT IS SHOWING UP FULL COLOR ON YOUR PAPER. Voila! That is it. Now the pen shouldn't "blob"!

These pens work if used properly. These, like other acrylic paint pens, require a little bit of prep before you use them. First, you want to gently press the nib inward, then you want to gently depress the nib several times (again, gently) until paint fills it.  Use a pen improperly, no matter the brand, and you will get paint blobs. A gentle hand and patience are the two magic tools here.When it comes to ease, Posca paint pens are just like holding a pen or a pencil. If you can do that, you'll be successful with these! They're very comfortable to hold in my hand and draw or write with. The flow of the paint is nice, and the colors are very vibrant and do no require more than one coat. I cannot speak of longevity, just yet, but depending on what you're painting with these, you should probably use some sort of sealer.The only thing I do not like about these markers is that they eat paper, it's not a big deal, certainly not a deal breaker for me, but it's definitely something I thought should be mentioned.These would make a great gift for yourself, or for the artists in your life.

Extremely nice, I really love these paint pens on paper or canvas. They work amazing on Canvas, but if you are using these on paper, it takes a bit of practice to get used to the techniques of using the pens without leaving any rough areas, flakes, etc.I have read a lot of reviews and a bunch of the negative ones seems to stem from the people not knowing HOW to use these paint pens on paper material since they are very absorbant. These paint pens are acrylic based so they dry extremely fast and very evenly.Just be sure to shake the pens (CAP SIDE UP, or it will leak all over) and then use a piece of scrap paper (make some lines) then pump the pen a few times, make some more lines (to prevent too much paint from pooling) BEFORE using them to draw on anything.DO NOT SHAKE THE PENS CAP SIDE DOWN. You aren't supposed to do this anyways with acrylic based paint pens from my experience, as the paint will leak into the tip from the force of the shaking. ALWAYS CAP SIDE UP.

There's a trick to getting these pens not to leak globs of paint everywhere when you first get them. You have to hold the pen with the point upwards, towards the ceiling, push the nib in with your finger, you'll hear a small amount of air escape, like a hissing sound. Then turn back over and press repeatedly onto paper to get the paint going. If you don't do this, globs will come out and go everywhere! Happened to me and lots of paint was wasted. But they work great once you get them going correctly.

ポスカは、本当に大好きな文房具です。ただ普通のサインペンとは違い、扱いにくい面もあります。そういったところも含めて自分はポスカが好きなのですが。　しばらく使わないときにほったらかしにしてしまうと、ペン先がカピカピに乾いてポンピングできなくなったり、インクが分離したりしますから、ポスカを効果的に使いたい人は、使わないときでも定期的に色出しやポンピングをし、コンディションの調整をした方がいいです。また、コンディションの良い状態のポスカは、振ってみたときに中の撹拌玉がカチャカチャと音を立てるはずです。もし音がしなかったら、それは中で沈殿したインクが固まっている証拠。そんな場合には、再びカチャカチャと音がしだすまで力強く振らなければなりません。もちろん、そうならないために定期的な使用が大切なのです。そしてポスカの場合、ペン立てにさして保管するのは愚の骨頂。必ず横にして保管しましょう。そうすることで、良いコンディションを保ちやすくなります。万が一、ペン先が固まって色が出なくなったり、ペン先がケバケバになっても、インクさえ残っていればペン先を交換することで復活します。替えのペン先が発売されています。以上が、15年ほどの使用歴で学んだ、効果的なポスカ使用のコツです。

**There is a "too long, didn't read" version at the bottom of this review**Disclosure: I am absolutely no stranger to paint markers. I am also no stranger to Uni Posca, and I decided to get a set of them because the last remaining one I had ran out of paint and the nib was getting pretty savage. This purchase is a lesson in consumer discretion because I should have read the 1 star reviews before purchasing, and here's why:So my package arrived 2 days early, without any updates on tracking info past "Shipped." "Oh cool, what a nice surprise" you may think. Naw, I had the misfortune of reading negative reviews beforehand saying these markers are gonna pool paint when pumping the valve and waste paint. I also kept track of the seller page and noticed the seller kept changing names (I bought from "japan-Container" but even to this day it keeps changing). I thought "surely these buyers are just being picky" because there were a lot of positive reviews compared to negative. Most of the positive reviews, if legitimate and non-bot, are clearly from beginners and hobbyists who haven't experimented with many paint markers and just settle for these out of ignorance. I should have just assumed they were bots/fake accounts from the beginning.As other people who have bought these and left a negative review have said: the markers dump paint out when you pump the nib down, even the first pump. On real Posca's, when you pump the nib down it juices the nib and primes it, just like with pretty much all other paint markers. But on these markers, even after the first pump it just dumps paint and pools at where the nib is. I can't put my finger on whether the nib is the incorrect size, the valve is jenky or if the paint is too thin... Either way, pretty much useless and I can't see myself using these markers on anything done professionally in the foreseeable future. I'm probably going to leave these markers alone until my Sharpie, Decocolor, Montana or Molotows run out of paint and could use more of a similar colour, otherwise i'll stick to familiar brands in the future. Hell, i'm even considering purchasing Molotow 227 empties just to use the Posca's paint.**Too Long, Didn't Read**Not real Uni Posca's, they are cheap knockoffs. Seller is non-responsive, shadey and routinely cycles through other sellers; tracking info is wildly inaccurate. Markers dump paint out when juicing the nib, even with pumping minimally. Spend the extra $ on purchasing locally or elsewhere.

I've been looking for marker pens that give a good, even coverage with no pen marks and can't be easily erased. Sadly, these pens don't fit that bill. However, there are other features of these pens that appeal instead.

To start with, these chunky pens are like marker pens, with a wide 8mm nib. You have to press the pen on a hard surface a few times to get the "ink" flowing, after shaking the pen until the internal ball is rattling loud and hard. Once the "ink" is running, you're good to go.

I keep using "ink" as the liquid that comes out of these pens isn't like ink but, instead, is more like thin poster paint. The finish is very matt, exactly like poster paint, and the colours are bright. You'll definitely want to try out the colours on a spare bit of paper to see exactly what the colours will look like; subtle they aren't. The ink/paint does seem permanent and does resist casual rubbing. Once dry, you can cover over with a different colour, but I've found that, as the ink/paint dries, it tends to curl the paper. So far, I've had to reverse curl the paper and put it under some books to get a flat finish. However, I do like the matt finish you get, but you can still see the "brush" marks.

These aren't the marker pens I was looking for, but they are the marker pens I would have been looking for next, purely for the matt finish and bright colours.

Not perfect, but a good alternative to the more common ink-based systems.

ポスカの購入が初めてなので、太さ・色合い・書き心地がどんなものかわからずバラ購入かセット購入かでもかなり迷いました。なのでこれから購入する方のために少しレビューしておきます。ポスカには現時点で太さが5種類あります。　極細(0.7mm)　細字(0.9～1.3mm)　中字(1.8～2.5mm)　太字(8.0mm)　極太(15.0mm)とりあえずお店で極細・細字・中字を1本ずつ買ってきて試しました。POP制作などA4くらいのサイズに大き目に描き込むなら「中字」が一番使い勝手良いですが、私はカードやハガキ等の小さなサイズに文字やイラストを描くのがメインなので「極細」にしました。細字で広範囲を塗り広げるのは可能でも逆に太字で細かい部分を描き込むのは不可能ですから。太さは誰もが知っている馴染みのあるペンで例えるとマッキーの極細と同じくらいです。細かい部分にも描き込みやすく、画数の多い漢字を小さめに書いてもインクでつぶれません。ベタ塗りは広い面積を塗ると時間がかかりますが2cm角くらいなら余裕でできます。ただし細い分、ペンの塗り跡が目立ちやすいのでインクの出を良くして軽い筆跡で塗るようにしています。色合いはほぼイメージ通りハッキリした基本色でした。必要な色だけバラ買いしても後々全色欲しくなってしまいそうなのでセットで購入。ケース付きなので持ち運びも管理もしやすいし早速使う予定のなかった色の出番があったので購入して良かったです。パステルカラーも出てるみたいなので必要に応じて増やしていこうと思います。ちなみにセット購入してもケースの中身はすべて一本ずつシュリンク梱包されているんですね。初めて使う時インクを出すのに時間がかかるペンなので使い始めの準備はけっこう面倒です…。

I received all 29 markers, all different colors like intended.A few people said these were dried out/used when they received them, but I'm not sure that's truly the case? If the nibs are white, they haven't been used at all, and I discovered they sometimes do take a little work to get the paint flowing.Also don't be an idiot and shake them with the cap off, that can cause paint splatter everywhere (I remembered the reviews with that and laughed, do none of you have common sense?).Anywho, when you're first "activating" them, you gotta shake them a bit while upside down, press the nib down against paper a few times, and shake a bit more, rinse and repeat until paint is saturating the nib. It doesn't work perfectly each time, sometimes takes a little extra work, but once they're working they are excellent! I tested all of mine and made sure they were working.The tips for the 5M markers are removable/reversable for cleaning/rinsing apparently, although the box does not give instructions nor mentions this (the USA Posca site DOES mention this, though, but they also have no instructions there either... I imagine it's just as simple as pulling the nib out, cleaning it, then slotting it back in? Unsure but I will test it later).I would highly recommend reading the FAQ on the Posca site if you have any curiosities about anything regarding the markers otherwise.

I have heard so many good things about Posca Pens, I decided to get some. I ordered a combined set that totaled 21 pens.

The first thing I didn't expect was that they were all individually shrink wrapped. Each pen. Whew, that took some time to get them all out of the wrapping.

The second thing I wasn't expecting is that you need to prime them the first time you use each pen. The first one just flooded out onto my paper. Don't shake more than a few times and then press the tip on the paper gently! You'll still have a small amount of paint come out, but not gushing. Don't prime on your work surface, prime on an extra sheet of paper. Otherwise you'll have a small puddle of paint on your work.

The next thing is that, although I did receive all 21 pens, I didn't get two of the colors that were listed, instead got two other colors in their place. Peach and Yellow Green were not included, instead I received Pink and Aqua Blue. That wasn't a big deal, there are enough colors that I won't miss the ones missing, and will use the substituted colors.

It took a while to figure out which colors I actually had because the writing on the packaging and on the pens is all in Japanese. I've seen some that are in English, and if I did this again, I'd definitely make sure I got pens with English. Since the colors aren't readable for me on the pens, I numbered each pen lid and made a chart in my sketchbook of the colors and numbers.

When I created this chart, I found that they pill up on textured watercolor paper. This was noted in other reviews I read, so I wasn't surprised.

All in all, now that I've primed all the pens and made my chart of colors and figured out what paper to use, I'm ready to go and think I will enjoy these pens. :) They really are a good price!

The paint can get quite messy if you're not careful and may run. Simply shake the marker a few times, push down the tip and write.I highly suggest doing a test run to get a feel for how they work before each go as the paint will blob on the first go. Once you start writing the paint comes out easily and is bright. Once it starts to turn sheer or isn't as white, give it a shake or push the tip again--but carefully.The box says "Extra Fine Tip" but I wouldn't call these extra fine by any means. It's also listed as 0.7mm which isn't really extra fine anyway; depending on how hard you push the pen could vary. I would say the tip is closer to 1 or 2mm though. The felt tip resembles a regular marker tip, but with some finesse you can make it "Fine".Using these on cardboard, paper, and opaque washi tape worked just fine.Overall, you get a very nice assortment for a great price and should last you a while depending on it's use.

Ich habe diese Stifte im Rahmen eines unbezahlten Produkttests ausgiebig testen dürfen. Als Illustratorin kommen mir schwarze Acrylstifte beinahe immer gelegen, da ich diese für alles Mögliche nutze: von schwarzen Hintergründen in Illustrationen bis zu besonders dunklen Stellen in Bildern oder einfach nur Beschriftungen. Mir ist dabei immer wichtig, dass die Stifte nicht dazu neigen zu tropfen und der Farbfluss relativ solide ist. Auch ein Abrubbeln der Spitze oder das schnelle Abnutzen dieser sind Dinge, die bei meinen Arbeitsmitteln No-Gos sind.Diese Stifte überzeugen durch Varianz und Qualität, schlagen also wirklich zwei Fliegen mit einer Klappe. Aufgrund der breiten Auswahl zwischen dünnen (beinahe zum Schreiben oder für Lineart geeigneten) Spitzen und richtig dicken Stiften ist wirklich alles dabei. In den drei Wochen, in denen ich diese auch wirklich regelmäßig beansprucht habe, kann ich zudem nicht von besagtem Tropfen oder einer übermäßigen Belastung der Spitze sprechen – und das, obwohl man natürlich hin und wieder mal nachpumpen muss!Je nach Papier muss man dabei natürlich sagen, dass nicht jeder Untergrund gleich gut geeignet ist, um mit Acrylmarkern darauf zu arbeiten. Ich habe für ein paar Beispielbilder einmal an einer alten Zeichnung in einem meiner Skizzenbücher nachgearbeitet und hier ist der schwarze Karton etwas empfindlich gewesen, da die Feuchtigkeit das Papier ein wenig angegriffen hat. Das liegt aber nicht an den Markern, denke ich. Trotzdem erwähne ich es hier, da die Marker auch Notizkleber aus Plastik angegriffen haben und diese Oberfläche abgelöst haben. Das kannte ich so noch nicht von Acryl, was ja eigentlich aus einer Basis von Pigmenten, nicht wieder ablösbarem Bindemittel und Wasser besteht. Ich vermute daher, dass das Bindemittel hier einfach etwas aggressiver ist und man eventuell bei Kindern darauf achten sollte, dass sie sich nicht mit den Stiften bemalen.Dennoch ist mein abschließendes Fazit rundum gut. Ich kann mit den Stiften gut arbeiten, sie sind bei mir nicht eingetrocknet und tun ihre Arbeit gut.

Dopo averli usati ogni giorno per una settimana ecco le mie considerazioni:Utilizzare per la prima volta i pennarelli, come tutti i marker di questa tipologia, richiede un po di pazienza. Bisogna scuotere per 30 secondi e poi premere ripetutamene la punta su un foglio fin quando si impregna finalmente la punta. Un po’ noioso ma necessario, anche i pennarelli più costosi e di marchi rinomati adottano lo stesso procedimento, tutto normale.Il colore nero risulta corposo e non sbava, asciuga rapidamente ma consiglio di mettere un supporto sotto il foglio se usate carta leggera tipo quelle da fotocopia perché potrebbe trasudare il colore dall’altro lato del foglio.Come potete vedere dalle foto i colori funzionano bene anche su supporti più ostili come una pietra ad esempio.Uso quotidianamente da una settimana la punta da 1 e 3 mm e ancora non si scarica. La durata dell’inchiostro sembra ottima. Inoltre il colore acrilico contenuto nei pennarelli è a base d’acqua quindi non è tossico e non contiene sostanze chimiche.Consiglio l’acquisto di questo prodotto sia ad amatori che professionisti. I pennarelli sono molto validi per il loro prezzo e la varietà delle punte è molto versatile per le più disparate esigenze. Consigliato!

My daughter is in heaven. Every kind of paint pen she could hope for is here: metallics, glitter, pastels, neon, and classic colors. All of the various categories worked as advertised. The glitter and metallic both sparkle, and while they're similar at a casual glance, the difference is there when you put them side by side (the metallics are more shine than shimmer). The glitter pens are also all true to color, not just 12 different labels on silver like others we've tried in the past. The neons jump off the page under UV light. They required less shaking than her previous favorite pens, and they go on smoothly. The tips are comparable to all the other fine pens she's had, and the pack includes spare replacement tips in case one breaks or wears out.

As for the packaging, I'm happy with it, but there are a few tiny things I could have wished for to make it perfect. The pens are numbered on the cap ends, but nowhere else on the pen barrels, so I had to warn my daughter not to separate the caps from the pens and only to ever use one pen at a time lest she mix them up. The legend is on the box, which is fine, as the box is very sturdy and designed for easy access, with the numbers clearly visible when the lid is removed, but there are no fixed dividers in the box to keep the pens from getting mixed up, and with 72 pens, them trying to slide around or fall under the weight of their neighbors when one or more pens have been removed is inevitable. They even arrived mixed up: we had to dump them out and sort them ourselves. Just putting in a few fixed dividers would have solved all of these problems. Especially as the product is broken into 12 pen sets, breaking the box into 12 pen compartments would have made so much more sense and taken a 9 star product to a 10. That's nitpicking, though, so I did not let it affect my rating.

Overall, these are a great product, and fully deserving of the premium price. I doubt I'll need to buy them again myself, these should last us a good long while, but I'll definitely be recommending them to our friends, and if she ever manages to use all of these up, I'll be back.

The lighter colors are somewhat transparent allowing you to create your own colors as well, but unless you let the bottom color dry completely (just a few moments) the bottom color will leave some color on the "brush" tip of the lighter one. The side has a window so you know how much paint is left. You need to shake them well and the bonus is you can also tell how well the paint is mixed by looking at the window. There is a mixing bead inside but some colors take more shaking than others to fully blend (like purples and grays). They come with swatch sheets in black & white as well as a printed swatch sheet. I'm glad they included the swatch sheets for you to make yourself because some of the colors came out lighter than the printed sheet. They write really smoothly and you can write slower to make sure the color is fully opaque if you don't want to wait for it to dry and do two coats. - inizialmente uscirà molto più inchiostro del normale, se dovete fare qualcosa di artistico vi consiglio di usarlo momentaneamente in brutta per far uscire l’inchiostro maggiore. Poco dopo la quantità di inchiostro si regolerà e sarà minore rendendo il tratto più fine (ma per me rimane comunque piuttosto grosso perciò non lo trovo fine come scritto in descrizione).

- se tenete la penna in posizione verticale smetterà di funzionare e per farla ripartire dovrete nuovamente agitarla o tenerla a lungo in posizione orizzontale. - su un’agenda normale il colore non trapassa ma dall’altra parte si noterà moltissimo. È più adatta da usare in fogli molto spessi o in situazioni in cui si ha intenzione di usare una sola facciata.

- ad asciugare su carta ci mette parecchio (minuti) e ci si sporca facilmente, oltre che a rovinare le scritte fatte

In conclusione,

- per disegni professionali credo siano troppo imprecise dato il continuo cambio di flusso di inchiostro se la di tiene verticale ecc
- per qualsiasi altro utilizzo dovrebbero essere invece adatta e consigliabile
